ABOUT FLAGSHIP PIONEERING 

 Flagship Pioneering is a platform innovation company that conceives, creates, resources, and develops first-in-category life sciences and technology companies. Since its founding in 2000, Flagship has originated over 100 scientific ventures and has deployed over $3 billion in capital toward the development of transformative life science businesses. Flagship's current portfolio of more than 35 companies includes Moderna, Generate Biomedicines, Sail Biomedicines, iris labs, and Extuitive.

 ABOUT FL127 

 FL127 is a privately held, early-stage company operating within the Flagship Pioneering ecosystem. The company is developing a first-in-category platform anchored in novel device technology. FL127 is building its scientific and technical foundation through a hypothesis-driven experimental program. We are assembling a lean team of scientists and engineers who work at the intersection of hardware, software, and physiology, and who want to build in an era when AI agents are first-class members of the team.

 THE ROLE 

 FL127 is seeking a scientist to help connect the physiological signals our platform measures to what they indicate about a person. You will ground each signal in physiology, help design the human studies that test what it reflects, and build models that relate our measurements to reference measures and outcomes in small human cohorts.

 Our imaging and signal-extraction team produces the measurements. Your work starts from those outputs. You will co-design human studies with that team so a single study informs both measurement quality and interpretation.

 FL127 is an AI-native company. Team members direct AI agents in their daily work for literature synthesis, study design, data analysis, and code. We are looking for someone who wants to work this way.

 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 

 
 Ground each measured signal in physiology: what it reflects, what confounds it, and which physiological states it may indicate

 Work with the product and market team to decide which applications to study first, weighing scientific plausibility, study cost, and user value

 Co-design human studies with the imaging team, including endpoints, reference measurements, and protocols

 Build and evaluate models that relate our measurements to reference measures and outcomes on small cohorts, with attention to confounders, leakage, demographic stratification, and sample size

 Set the evidence bar a finding must meet before it shapes the product, and report what the data supports and where it falls short

 Review extracted signals for physiological plausibility and suggest improvements to the measurement pipeline

 
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 PhD in biomedical engineering, physiology, bioengineering, biophotonics, or a related field, or an MD/PhD, with substantial applied machine learning experience

 Deep knowledge of human physiology in an area such as microcirculation, hemodynamics, tissue optics, skin biology, or cardiorespiratory physiology

 Experience taking a measurement or digital biomarker through human studies, including endpoint selection, reference measurements, IRB-governed protocols, and agreement analysis

 Statistical modeling on small human datasets, including within-subject and longitudinal designs

 Proficiency in Python and the modern ML stack, and comfort working inside an existing research codebase

 Enough imaging and signal-processing background to reason about how calibration, registration, and sampling affect a derived measurement

 Ability to work independently in an early-stage, ambiguous environment and make decisions with incomplete data

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 Published or applied work in remote physiological sensing, digital biomarkers, or wearable or contactless measurement

 Experience turning research results into a product feature, ideally at a consumer device company

 Familiarity with skin optics models (Monte Carlo simulation, diffusion theory, chromophore decomposition)

 Experience modeling individual baselines and change over time

 Experience in a venture-backed startup or early-stage research environment

 
 WHY FL127 

 
 Work with human study data from your first weeks

 Shape which applications the company studies and builds first

 Join a small team where scientists and AI agents work side by side

 Draw on the scientific, operational, and capital resources of the Flagship Pioneering ecosystem

 
 
  

 Privacy Notice for Applicants:  When you apply for a role at Flagship Pioneering or one of its portfolio companies, we collect and use personal information you provide (such as your name, contact details, work history, and application materials) to evaluate your application, communicate with you, and comply with legal obligations. Your application data is processed through Greenhouse, our applicant tracking system, and may also be reviewed using AI-assisted screening tools. We do not sell your personal information. California residents have rights under the CCPA/CPRA including to know, delete, and opt out of the sharing of their personal information. If you are located in the EU or UK, we process your data under GDPR and you have rights to access, rectify, and erase your data. To exercise your rights or for questions, contact privacy@flagshippioneering.com. 



 The salary range for this role is $136,000 - $211,750. Compensation for the role will depend on a number of factors, including a candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies, and experience. FL127 currently offers healthcare coverage, annual incentive program, retirement benefits and a broad range of other benefits.
